## Root cause

In `source/cclib/parser/orcaparser.py`, the absorption/emission spectrum block parsed every transition-property table (electric dipole, velocity dipole, combined multipole, SOC-corrected, X-ray, CASSCF) and then unconditionally did `set_attribute('etenergies', ...)` / `set_attribute('etoscs', ...)` per table. Since ORCA prints the velocity-dipole table after the electric-dipole table, the exported `etoscs` ended up holding velocity-gauge numbers (fixture: `0.0002, 0.0861, 0.0045`) instead of the canonical transition-electric-dipole oscillator strengths (`0.0056, 1.1654, 0.0312`). Finite and non-empty, but scientifically wrong — exactly the reported inconsistency.

## Fix (`orcaparser.py:1281-1293`)

The exported `etenergies`/`etoscs` now come from the canonical `ABSORPTION SPECTRUM VIA TRANSITION ELECTRIC DIPOLE MOMENTS` table. Every parsed spectrum is still stored in `transprop` keyed by its header, and tables are used as a fallback for the exported attributes only when no canonical table exists (e.g. CASSCF `ABSORPTION SPECTRUM`, ROCIS SOC-corrected, or X-ray-only output). No fixture values, names-as-data, or line numbers are hard-coded — the rule is keyed on the table identity/ordering, so it generalizes across variants and version layouts.
